title: Billing & Quota Discrepancy Triage and Customer Communication Playbook
author: Marina Alvarez
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the end-to-end triage, technical investigation, remediation, and customer communications process for billing and quota discrepancies reported by enterprise, dedicated, and private tenants. It covers initial intake, data collection, technical verification, remediation options (including safe-mode and temporary caps), crediting thresholds, and the escalation matrix when there is suspected metering, aggregation, or accounting system error.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Resolve customer-reported billing or quota issues quickly while preserving trust and avoiding unnecessary credits.
- Scope: Applies to all enterprise and Dedicated/Private tenants. Does not replace formal legal billing dispute processes if requested by finance; instead this playbook prepares evidence for finance handoff.
- Out-of-scope: One-off developer test accounts on self-serve plans (handled by Growth Support).

Owner and Roles:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (owner_team).
- Technical lead: Oncall Observability Engineer (eng-platform / eng-sre on rotation).
- Billing coordinator: Revenue Ops / Billing team (finance-legal).
- Communications owner: Customer Success AM or Technical Account Manager (TAM).
- Escalation contacts: SRE Pager (pager duty), Billing Ops Slack channel (#billing-ops), Legal counsel (only invoked for formal disputes).

SLA expectations (customer-facing):
1) Acknowledgement: 1 business hour during business hours (M-F 08:00–18:00 local).
2) Triage update: within 6 hours with next steps and ETA for investigation.
3) Technical findings: within 24 hours for straightforward cases; up to 72 hours for cross-system investigations.
4) Temporary mitigation or credit decision: within 3 business days for high-impact outages; 7 business days for complex disputes requiring finance/legal review.

Intake checklist (what the support engineer/TAM must capture at first contact):
- Customer report summary (short): how the discrepancy was discovered and customer impact.
- Tenant identifier (tenant_id), account id, contract #, billing cycle, affected date/time window.
- Examples: Request IDs, timestamps, sample requests/responses, and any exported telemetry the customer has.
- Quota measure: type of quota (concurrent requests, daily token budget, embedding units, dedicated GPU-hours) and expected vs observed values.
- Billing issue type: overcharge, missing charge, incorrect tier, double-billing, credit not applied, invoice mismatch.
- Permission to pull account-level logs and invoices (confirm customer consent where required).

Initial technical verification steps (engineer):
1) Reproduce the reported symptom on internal dashboards where possible. Check tenant-level metrics: ingress token count, egress, request count, peak concurrency.
2) Compare telemetry across three sources: API gateway logs, serving runtime metering, and billing aggregation pipeline (ETL).
3) Verify timezones and billable windows; many disputes come from timezone misalignment and daylight savings.
4) Check for recent model rollouts, canaries, or bulk ingest jobs that could spike usage.
5) If rate-limited or throttled: verify whether client retries inflated apparent request counts (see retry amplification section below).

Important commands and paths (internal):
- Fetch tenant metrics (CLI): redwood-metrics query --tenant <tenant_id> --from <ISO> --to <ISO> --metrics tokens,requests,embeddings
- Pull serving logs (K8s): kubectl -n tenant-<id> logs deployment/ingress-proxy --since=72h | grep <tenant_id>
- Billing pipeline debug: billing-tools fetch-aggregate --tenant <tenant_id> --cycle <YYYY-MM> --output json
- Correlate request -> invoice: correlate-requests --requests-file requests.json --billing-file billing_aggregate.json --out correlation_report.json

Common root causes and detection heuristics:
- Retry amplification: large client retries (short client backoff) cause repeated billable requests; detection: identical payloads with short (<5s) spacing from same source IP and client_id.
- Dual-ingress misconfiguration: tenant traffic routed via two ingress endpoints (e.g., edge+proxy) resulting in double-counting. Detect via mismatched request IDs across gateways.
- Billing ETL lag or late-arriving events: billing aggregate missing streaming events until next window. Detect via delta between real-time runtime counters and billing aggregate for same window.
- Timezone/window mismatch: Customer expecting UTC but invoice uses customer local timezone.
- Quota assignment errors: customer migrated between SKUs and quota assignment did not update. Detect by comparing tenant record in Account DB vs Quota Service.

Mitigations and remediation paths:
- Immediate safe-mode: apply temporary quota cap or soft throttle to prevent further spend while investigating. Steps: Customer Success -> Confirm with customer -> Apply cap using admin console -> Notify SRE and Billing.
- Temporary credit provisional: For high-impact customers where a suspected metering bug exists, provision a provisional credit (up to $X or N% of disputed amount) pending final reconciliation. Finance must be notified for credits > $5k.
- Recompute and replay billing window: Re-run ETL with corrected inputs or use the reconciliation tool to regenerate invoice for the affected period.
- Rollback configuration changes: If a recently deployed routing or metering change caused double-counting, rollback the change via standard deploy rollback runbook and re-process billing events.

Escalation matrix (when to escalate):
- Level 1 (Support Engineer): handles routine mismatches and data collection.
- Level 2 (SRE / Observability): escalate if root cause requires log-level correlation or cluster-level replay.
- Level 3 (Billing Ops): escalate for invoice regeneration, formal credits, legal notices.
- Level 4 (Executive / Legal): escalate when customer demands formal dispute, regulatory implication, or credit > $50k.

Severity mapping and action table:
| Severity | Customer impact | Priority | Target action | Owner |
| P0 | Service offline or runaway spend causing major business impact | Urgent | Acknowledge 1h; safe-mode; exec notify; provisional credit | Support + SRE + Finance |
| P1 | Significant unexpected spend or quota exhaustion impacting core flows | High | Acknowledge 1h; mitigate with cap; technical investigation 24h | Support + SRE |
| P2 | Moderate discrepancy or invoice mismatch with low immediate impact | Medium | Investigate 72h; prepare evidence for billing ops | Support |
| P3 | Cosmetic or minor invoice rounding differences | Low | Document and correct on next invoice cycle | Support/Billing Ops |

Customer communication templates (short examples):
- Initial acknowledgement (1 hour):
  "Hi <Customer>, thank you for reporting this. We have opened ticket RED-<id> and will investigate. We will provide an update within 6 hours. Could you please confirm the tenant_id and attach any example request IDs or invoice line items? -- <TAM>"

- Update after initial verification (6 hours):
  "Update: We verified that X tokens were recorded in runtime vs Y in billing aggregate for window <time>. We are re-running the billing reconcile and have applied a temporary cap to prevent further unexpected spend. Next update by <ETA>. -- <TAM>"

- Resolution and credit summary: 
  "Resolution: Root cause was <cause>. We have regenerated the invoice for <period> and applied a credit of $<amount> to your account. The corrected invoice is attached. If you prefer, we can arrange a follow-up call to review details. -- <Billing Ops>"

Audit evidence required for Finance handoff:
- Correlation report (request -> billing line).
- Raw logs for sampled requests (timestamps, request_ids, tenant_id).
- ETL run IDs and commit hashes if a code change is suspected.
- Internal incident timeline and mitigation actions.

Retry amplification guidance (preventative):
- Recommend that customers use exponential backoff with capped retries and idempotency tokens for non-idempotent operations.
- For high-volume ingest jobs, encourage batch APIs that are cheaper and reduce per-request accounting.

Operational runbook snippets (step-by-step):
1) Intake: Create ticket, record all intake checklist items, assign P0/P1/P2/P3.
2) Triage: Run quick reconciliation scripts and capture delta.
3) Mitigate: If runaway spend, apply safe-mode cap and notify account.
4) Investigate: Pull logs, run correlation, reproduce if possible.
5) Remediate: Recompute invoice or rollback offending release.
6) Communicate: Use templates. Confirm final credit and close ticket after finance sign-off.

Post-incident actions and telemetry improvements (retrospective):
- If root cause is internal: open engineering ticket to fix meter or ETL bug, include test cases and synthetic workload to reproduce.
- If caused by customer behavior: create guidance for the customer and update onboarding docs to include recommended retry/backoff and suggested quotas.
- Add or refine synthetic monitors that compare runtime live counters with billing aggregates and auto-alert on >5% drift for any tenant for a 12-hour sliding window.

Metrics to track for this playbook's effectiveness:
- Mean time to acknowledgement (target < 1 hour).
- Mean time to provisional mitigation (target < 6 hours for P0/P1).
- % disputes resolved without finance credit (target 60% where correction is internal).
- False positives in synthetic monitor (target < 2% per month).

Appendix A: Example correlation command usage
- Example: redwood-metrics query --tenant 98765 --from 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-05-02T00:00:00Z --metrics tokens,requests > /tmp/98765_runtime.json
- Example reconciliation: correlate-requests --requests-file /tmp/98765_runtime.json --billing-file /tmp/98765_billing.json --out /tmp/correlation_98765.json

Appendix B: Sample temporary customer-facing email for P0
"""
Subject: Immediate action taken on your account — temporary cap applied and investigation underway

Hi <Customer Name>,

We have applied a temporary spend cap to your account to stop any further unexpected charges and begun a full investigation. Our support ticket is RED-<id>. We will update you within one hour with the current findings and next steps. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

If you would like immediate contact, reply to this email and we will arrange a call.

Best,
<Your TAM>
"""

Document maintenance:
- Review cadence: quarterly.
- Last review: 2026-06-10. Next review target: 2026-09-10.
